create.title: Exact high-shell hyperbola-floor Fourier reduction and target-safe endpoint residual
create.statement_tex: Let Y=R^2 asymp sqrt(X), let J=[A,B] intersect Z lie in [cY,CY] with ell=B-A+1<=R, and restrict R/4<h<=R/2. Put L_h=(A+h-1)/(2h), U_h=(B+h)/(2h), q_h=2floor(L_h)+1, and nu_h=floor(U_h)-floor(L_h) in {0,1,2}. With I_1(v)=v(3-v)/2, I_2(v)=v(v-1)/2, and the exact actual starred amplitude, the complete row is (-1)^floor(L_h){I_1(nu_h)F_h(q_h)-I_2(nu_h)F_h(q_h+2)}. The character zero mode cancels only with both Abel boundaries and all differences, while the geometric selector mode ell/(2h) remains. For every endpoint argument t_h=(N+ch)/(dh), N asymp R^2 and d in {2,4}, the floor-compatible Vaaler residual satisfies sum_h kappa_T(t_h)<<_epsilon X^epsilon(R/T+1): if ||t_h||<=delta, then s=N-(dk-c)h has |s|<<delta R and h divides N-s, giving X^epsilon(delta R+1) samples. Thus T=ceil(sqrt(R)) makes the full endpoint and integer-jump residual target-sized. The finite core is exactly sum_(A<=n<=B)e(sqrt(Xn)) sum_(h|n,R/4<h<=R/2,n/h odd) chi_4(n/h) Atilde_X(h,n/h). Fixed-floor branches and fixed-q fibres have O(1) points, and modewise or branchwise absolute closure retains R capacity versus sqrt(R), sharp on the inherited actual fourth-power unmatched family. This is not a signed lower bound; the short actual-symbol twisted-divisor estimate remains open.

reject.reason: On a two-point row the unweighted character count is zero, whereas the actual contribution is a phase- and amplitude-weighted difference that can have order-one size.
The character mean cancels only with the complete Abel boundary ledger. The geometric count mode ell/(2h) remains in the exact selector.
The target-safe Fejer residual leaves a finite core whose branchwise and modewise absolute capacity is R, sharp on the accepted actual fourth-power unmatched family, against target sqrt(R).
Large real frequency does not control its fractional derivative; exact fourth-power odd-divisor incidences exhibit reciprocal-frequency collisions modulo one.

The audited Robert-Sargos mapping retains a full-box term of the wrong size, and Duke-Friedlander-Iwaniec requires modular inverses, coprimality, and smooth weights absent from the floor-selected actual symbol.

no_change.reason: The signed high-shell twisted-divisor core, lower h sector, and alpha transfer remain open.
The exact reduction and residual theorem prove no new discrepancy exponent.

round_assessment.reason: Round 58 proves an exact complete-row floor representation and a sharper divisor-sampled Fejer residual bound that closes all endpoint approximation error at the target scale. It isolates the sole high-shell survivor as a signed short actual-symbol twisted-divisor sum and rules out branchwise, modewise-absolute, spacing-only, and presently cited black-box closures. No shell estimate or exponent is proved.
